raw_case_text: A 11 year-old child was referred to our department with a 1 month history of pain in the right chest. In his past history, he had a surgery of hydatid cyst of the liver three years ago. A physical examination revealed a diminution of the breath sound in the upper right lobe without other clinical sign, and the patient was in excellent condition. The chest X-ray realised in our patient showed right upper lobe opacity (Figure 1) and the first diagnosis suspected, within his past history and endemic aspect of hydatid disease in our region was a hydatid cyst of the lung. The patient was operated and we discovered tissular mass invading upper lobe with suspect parietal contact, we performed a complete resection of the mass with dorsal right upper lobe segmentectomy and resection of parietal pleural beside the tumour., The diagnosis of askin's tumor was established histological (Figure 2) on the presence of small cells with scant cytoplasm and focal necrosis, the cells were round and had scant cytoplasm with inconspicuous nucleoli. Mitotic figures were numerous. Rosettes were only focally identified, and immunohistochemistry objective that the tumor cells is positive for neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and CD99. Our patient receives adjuvant chemoradiotherapy with good evolution. Two years after the patient died with lung, liver and bone metastasis.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 11-year-old child presented with a 1-month history of right-sided chest pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The child was referred for a 1-month history of right chest pain without constitutional deterioration.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underwent surgical excision of a hepatic hydatid cyst 3 years earlier; resided in a hydatid-endemic region.

objective.physical_examination: Excellent general condition; respiratory examination revealed diminished breath sounds over the right upper lung lobe without other abnormalities.
objective.routine_investigations: Chest X-ray demonstrated a dense opacity in the right upper lung lobe, initially suspected to be a pulmonary hydatid cyst.
objective.advanced_workup: Thoracotomy revealed a solid tissue mass invading the right upper lobe with parietal pleural adherence, treated via dorsal right upper lobe segmentectomy and parietal pleurectomy. Histopathology demonstrated sheets of small round cells with scant cytoplasm, inconspicuous nucleoli, numerous mitoses, focal necrosis, and focal Homer-Wright rosettes; immunohistochemistry was positive for CD99 and neuron-specific enolase (NSE).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Thoracopulmonary malignant small round cell tumor (Askin's tumor / primitive neuroectodermal tumor) in a child with prior hepatic hydatid cyst surgery, confirmed by histopathology and CD99/NSE immunohistochemical positivity (ruling out pulmonary hydatid cyst). Despite complete surgical resection and adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, the patient died 2 years later from pulmonary, hepatic, and osseous metastases.
